scope: Re-run of local.library_compatibility.20261027, whose raw reports were lost: scripts/qualify_library_compatibility.py on a frozen Debug build of 2d5aa7c (D:/wp/b65), 41/41 steps; owned TIA V21 scratch projects: a Bool-only FB type and an FB type using LInt/LWord/LTime are authored and released 1.0.0 on a CPU 1511-1 PN and archived in a global library. In a consumer scratch with an added CPU 1214C DC/DC/DC: (1) library_upgrade of TIA's own shipped native V13 library (Predefined-Styles.al13) is refused before any native call (LibraryVersionUnsupported) and the copied source tree stays byte-identical. (2) A compiled, unsaved source change is pending; the library_instantiate preview reports unsavedTargetEdits {present: true, disposition: savedIntoCheckpointBaseline}, the apply saves it into the checkpoint baseline, and a fresh reopen contains both the edit and the instance. (3) A type whose source generation fails is discarded by TIA (EngineeringError, not in memory); a valid PLC data type generated with compile=false is inconsistent (isConsistent false) and library_instantiate is refused before any checkpoint or write (InheritedDiagnostics) with the native inventory unchanged; the reopen proves both types were discarded. (4) Into the S7-1200 the Bool-only type instantiates and compiles with 0 errors; the 64-bit type is checkpointed and instantiated but fails compilation (CompileFailed, 8 errors: LInt/LWord/LTime unknown on the CPU), completes no save, and a fresh reopen equals the saved inventory before the attempt. 41/41 steps.
limitations: No V20 library input exists on this PC, so V20 upgrades stay open until one is obtained. V14 SP1-V18 upgrades are covered by local.library_upgrades.20261024 and the five DMC V19 archives by local.library_vendor.20261024/20261025.
The V13 input is TIA's own shipped HMI style library; it is refused by version before any native call.

The unsaved edit is a compiled, unsaved source change; arbitrary unsaved user edits in an attached TIA UI are not reproduced. The inherited inconsistency is an uncompiled PLC data type; other inconsistent object kinds are not exercised.

Only CPU family is varied (S7-1500 to S7-1200, newest catalog firmware); the CPU-family mismatch surfaces as CompileFailed after checkpoint, not as a refusal at preparation. Firmware-version mismatches are not exercised. No runtime execution.
